about: Ground truth for the W3C BAD demo pages (Before and After: home, tickets, survey; News excluded), written in our own short wording from W3C's annotated pages, citing W3C note numbers. Only keyboard and focus barriers are labelled. Template notes say errors on the template propagate to every page, so template keyboard notes are labelled on each of the three pages. status 'failure' is a documented barrier on a Before page; 'clean' is the same row on the After page, which W3C documents as repaired. types are the failure types that match the row (vocabulary below). carrier_ids are DOM ids of the elements that carry it, carrier_tags a tag a walker finding may carry when the elements have no id or name, carrier_names visible names a model answer may use; empty lists mean the row is matched by type alone. walk_exercised says whether a Tab, Enter and Escape walk can show the barrier at all.

types.focus-order: Tab order does not follow the visual order
types.focus-not-moved: after something opens, focus is not moved into it
types.focus-not-returned: after something closes, focus does not return to its trigger
types.keyboard-trap: focus cannot leave a part of the page with the keyboard
types.not-focusable: an interactive element cannot be reached with Tab
types.focus-not-visible: the focused element shows no visible focus indicator
types.focus-obscured: the focused element is hidden by other content
types.no-bypass: no skip link or other way to bypass repeated blocks
types.keyboard-operation: a control is hard to operate with the keyboard or acts on its own while the keyboard moves through it
types.other: any other keyboard or focus failure
